summary_paragraph: A 31-year-old woman with a history of bronchopulmonary dysplasia from prematurity and chronic tracheostomy was admitted for progressive dyspnea and evaluation of her airway. She underwent a rigid bronchoscopy with replacement of her tracheostomy tube to a fenestrated, uncuffed Portex tube. Postoperatively, she developed hoarseness and was found to have supraglottic edema and laryngitis, likely fungal (laryngeal thrush), for which she was started on fluconazole. GERD management was intensified with omeprazole. Her voice improved with rest, and she was discharged home on day four with instructions to continue trach care, complete the antifungal course, and follow up as an outpatient. Thoracic surgery recommended further work-up for long-term management.
